page: Amazon Web Services m6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of up to 3.6 GHz. The memory subsystem consists of 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration supporting AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

In computational benchmarks, the AMD EPYC architecture exhibits strong single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng evaluations, ranking in the top quartile, alongside solid mid-tier multi-core computing metrics such as a PassMark CPU score of 23501.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9646.0. Memory subsystem testing shows average throughput for small cached blocks at 1139.89 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidths dip into the lower quartile at 38.43 GB/sec and 21.76 GB/sec respectively. Synthetic web and database tests show steady throughput, yielding 16.06 GB/sec in static web serving and 17.77 million operations per second for Redis SET commands.

The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent file systems, and it incorporates a baseline network speed of 6 Gbps without hardware GPU acceleration. By balancing 16 virtual processing cores with 64 GB of memory, m6a.4xlarge offers a balanced resource ratio suitable for application servers, microservices clusters, mid-tier relational databases, continuous integration pipelines, and general enterprise container workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server utilizing x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processors running at 3.6 GHz. It offers 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, combined with 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, adhering to a balanced 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks integrated local storage, depending entirely on remote storage volumes, and offers a baseline network capacity of 6 Gbps without GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core stress-ng performance, accompanied by average multi-core processing, static web serving throughput of 16.06 GB/sec, and steady Redis key-value operations at 17.77 million operations per second. Its resource configuration makes it appropriate for backend web serving, build runners, distributed microservices, and general-purpose database hosting.
